purpose: Define the future comparative and statistical analysis layer for evaluating re-planning policies, solver-backed techniques, internal baselines, and delay propagation behavior under controlled dynamic TRSP and WSRP experiments.

problem_family: field operations with technicians, tasks, routes, time windows, and operational disruptions
research_alignment.dissertation_scope: Delay propagation remains the first dissertation focus. Other perturbations may be supported later by the platform, but they are not required for the first defensible academic contribution.
research_alignment.central_question: Given a problem class and a delay scenario, compare which re-planning policy or technique is more appropriate considering performance, robustness, stability, feasibility, service level, and computational cost.
research_alignment.decision_framework_goal: Convert repeated experimental evidence into a replicable recommendation method for selecting a re-planning policy or technique.

comparison_unit.reason: Policies must be compared under equivalent conditions. A single isolated run is not enough to support a scientific conclusion.

candidate_policy_families.label: No re-planning baseline
candidate_policy_families.role: Reference policy used to quantify the damage caused by delays when no corrective action is taken.

candidate_policy_families.label: Threshold-based delay re-planning
candidate_policy_families.role: Simple interpretable policy for triggering re-planning only when delay impact crosses predefined thresholds.

candidate_policy_families.label: Solver-backed re-planning
candidate_policy_families.role: Future optimization-backed policy family. It should use an adapter boundary instead of hardcoding one solver into the research workflow.

candidate_policy_families.label: Hybrid or metaheuristic re-planning
candidate_policy_families.role: Future technique family for larger or time-constrained scenarios where exact or constraint-based approaches may be too costly.

ranking_analysis: summarize tradeoffs instead of hiding them behind one score
statistical_analysis_plan.minimum_scientific_rule: Do not claim one policy is globally better from a single run, a single instance, or a single metric.

quality_requirements: Every comparison must identify the instance, perturbation scenario, policy, and metric set.
Every policy ranking must preserve the metrics that caused the ranking.
Every statistical conclusion must state whether it is descriptive, paired, sensitivity-based, or only exploratory.
Every future solver-backed result must report solver status and computational cost.
Every recommendation must remain tied to a scenario class instead of pretending to be universal.
safety_requirements: Do not expose comparative experiment execution from the browser yet.
Do not claim operational deployment readiness from static samples or contracts.
Do not hide failed runs, infeasible results, timeout cases, or solver warnings.
Do not mix policies tested under different perturbations as if they were paired comparisons.
Do not use statistical output as proof of real company performance before external validation.
conservative_note: This contract defines the future comparative analysis layer. It does not execute experiments, run solvers, perform statistical tests, mutate schedules, write results, or trigger backend jobs from the web interface.
